meeting_header:
Date: 2027-03-15
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Grace Thompson (CTO - Elysia), Ibrahim Noor (ML Eng - Elysia), Lena Ortiz (Product - Elysia)
summary: Discovery call to understand Elysia's embeddings + reranking needs. Customer evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private Redwood deployments. Key concerns: throughput / QPS, vector dimensionality and storage, hybrid search (BM25 + embeddings), vector DB integration (Pinecone/Weaviate/OpenSearch), security/compliance, and cost. Agreed next steps: pricing, security docs, schedule SE deep-dive and benchmarking plan.
transcript:
[00:00:00] Sofia Patel: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we can do quick intros and then dive into your current infra and goals
[00:00:08] Grace Thompson: hey thanks, i'm grace, cto at elysia, we build a search product for medical literature, so privacy and latency are big for us
[00:00:14] Ibrahim Noor: ibrahim here, ml eng, i'm running our embedding pipelines and currently evaluating rerank flows
[00:00:18] Lena Ortiz: lena, product — mostly here to hear tradeoffs and timeline
[00:00:22] Marcus Li: marcus from redwood, i'm the solutions eng, i'll go pretty deep on throughput and vector db integration
[00:00:26] Sofia Patel: great. quick agenda, confirm goals, current stack, constraints, then go over hosting modes — hosted api, dedicated, private — and talk about embeddings dimensionality and hybrid rerank
[00:00:40] Grace Thompson: sounds good
[00:00:43] Sofia Patel: do you want to start with current stack ibrahim?
[00:00:47] Ibrahim Noor: yeah, so currently we compute 768-d embeddings using a fine-tuned open model, about 3.5M docs, average vector per doc is 1.2, so ~4.2M vectors, qps right now is spiky — baseline is 25 qps but we see peaks to 200 during index refreshes and launches. We use pinecone for prod, although we've been prototyping with opensearch and weaviate internally
[00:01:12] Marcus Li: okay that gives a sense. what is your rerank flow — do you do a two-stage retrieval, bm25 then embed-rerank, or directly nearest-neighbor?
[00:01:22] Ibrahim Noor: two-stage mostly. bm25 to get top 200, then embed-based rerank on the top results. want to keep recall high but latencies under 250ms ideally for end-users
[00:01:32] Lena Ortiz: and cost is another constraint, we can't triple infra spend to get latency improvements
[00:01:37] Grace Thompson: and for compliance — SOC 2 is must, we might need on-prem for some clients later, so interested in dedicated and private options
[00:01:45] Sofia Patel: noted. quick question on vector dims — you said 768. have you experimented with 128 or 512 for cost/throughput tradeoffs?
[00:01:55] Ibrahim Noor: we did a quick PCA reduction to 256 and the qa dropped a bit, but we haven't tried 512. we're worried about index size with full 768 and maintenance windows
[00:02:06] Marcus Li: that's common. Redwood's optimize tooling can recommend quantization/resize profiles per workload; for Dedicated we can run a comparison at 128/256/512/768 to show latency & recall impact. for hosted api, tokenization and embedding pipelines are managed but you pay per vector store and per embed call
[00:02:26] Grace Thompson: what about hybrid search? we want BM25+Emb + some metadata filtering — does redwood support pipelined hybrid queries if we host vector DB separately?
[00:02:36] Marcus Li: yes, we do hybrid. we often do the retrieval in the vector db (or via our routing layer) and then run rerank in the runtime. if you host your own vector DB like weaviate or opensearch, we can route to it and bring embeddings back into Redwood for rerank; alternately Redwood Dedicated can host the indexing and rerank path to reduce network hops
[00:02:56] Ibrahim Noor: network hops are big for us — right now pinecone adds about 50-80ms on average for read, which eats into our 250ms SLO
[00:03:05] Marcus Li: with Dedicated in the same VPC and region we see sub-10ms for local NVLink isn't applicable here but network adjacency matters; for private deployments on-prem you can collocate to get similar numbers
[00:03:16] Sofia Patel: do you have requirements around data residency or KMS?
[00:03:19] Grace Thompson: yes some customers require data never leaves their VPC, and we need KMS integration for key rotation, plus audit logs per request
[00:03:28] Marcus Li: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and audit logging; Dedicated also supports KMS integration and private networking. we'll include SOC 2 and the audit logging config in the security pack
[00:03:39] Lena Ortiz: curious about throughput — if we move rerank into redwood dedicated, what QPS can we expect for 512-dim vs 768-dim at p95 latency target of 200ms?
[00:03:50] Marcus Li: rough back-of-envelope: on a Dedicated 4-GPU pool optimized for inference, with batching we can do around 300-500 qps for a 512-dim rerank call at p95 under 200ms depending on batch windows; 768 will be lower, maybe 180-300 qps. those numbers vary a lot with sequence length and rerank model size. we should run your dataset through a benchmark to be precise
[00:04:13] Ibrahim Noor: that aligns with what we were expecting. also how does caching work? we have lots of repeated queries for the same top docs during conferences, would caching help reduce cost?
[00:04:22] Marcus Li: yes, prefix and result caching helps — Redwood caches kv prefixes and rerank outputs for short TTLs. plus cold-starts can be handled by warmup policies. caching can cut token cost significantly for repeated queries
[00:04:33] Grace Thompson: on storage — how big would 4.2M vectors be for 768 versus 512 when stored in Dedicated? raw float32 vs quantized?
[00:04:43] Marcus Li: rough math: 4.2M * 768 * 4 bytes ~ 12.9 GB? wait that's off, sorry let me calc — 4,200,000 * 768 * 4 bytes = about 12.9 TB actually, oh man my quick math slip; it's tens of GB per million — let me be precise later. with 512 and 8-bit quant you can reduce by ~4x. Redwood's optimize reports will show disk and memory footprints per quantization profile
[00:05:03] Ibrahim Noor: yeah storage is major, especially with replication and backups. we need to know expected index sizes for the Dedicated plan
[00:05:10] Sofia Patel: we'll include estimated storage + network egress in the pricing doc. any regulatory constraints like HIPAA?
[00:05:15] Grace Thompson: some customers are in healthcare, so HIPAA is a maybe; we need the private option for those clients
[00:05:20] Marcus Li: understood — Private on-prem or VPC deployments are common for HIPAA customers; we can share compliance artifacts
[00:05:27] Lena Ortiz: what's the migration effort from pinecone -> redwood dedicated? we don't want downtime during cutover
[00:05:33] Marcus Li: migration patterns: snapshot export from pinecone, ingest into Redwood or your vector DB in a staging VPC, warm caches and gradually shift traffic via routing policies. we can do a canary rollout by 10% increments to control risk
[00:05:47] Ibrahim Noor: do you support custom distance metrics? our experiments use cosine mostly, but one team wants dot-product for some scoring pipelines
[00:05:55] Marcus Li: yes we support cosine, dot-product, and L2. routing and transform layers can normalize scores if needed. when using hybrid bm25 + embed, we often normalize similarity scores before rerank to keep the scale consistent
[00:06:08] Grace Thompson: any limits on vector dimensionality? our embedding provider might go to 1024 in future
[00:06:13] Marcus Li: no hard cap, but higher dims increase memory and compute linearly; beyond 768 you'll see throughput drop and storage increase. we recommend doing a cost-quality sweep with representative queries
[00:06:25] Sofia Patel: let's talk about pricing briefly — hosted api is simplest but can be more expensive at scale, dedicated gives predictable throughput and cost savings with reserved capacity, private has larger one-time deployment costs
[00:06:36] Grace Thompson: can you give a back-of-envelope? we currently pay pinecone + our compute, and it's about $Xk/month; want to know if dedicated will save us 30%+ before we commit
[00:06:45] Sofia Patel: we'll run a TCO model for you and show break-even based on your QPS and storage. i'll include reserved capacity tiers and burst options
[00:06:54] Lena Ortiz: security review — we'd need SSO, RBAC and per-route audit logs. also retention controls for vectors generated from user-submitted content
[00:07:03] Marcus Li: all supported — SSO via SAML/OIDC, RBAC, per-route retention TTLs. we also have redact and retention hooks for embeddings generated from PII data
[00:07:14] Ibrahim Noor: curious about model variants — if capacity is constrained, would redwood automatically fall back to smaller model for rerank? we don't want a sudden quality drop without visibility
[00:07:24] Marcus Li: yes fallback policies are configurable; you can do A/B or canary rollouts and automatic fallback to a compatible variant. Redwood Console shows per-route traces and quality regressions so you can set alerts
[00:07:36] Grace Thompson: timeline — if we decide to pilot, what's a realistic timeline to run benchmarks and a short pilot?
[00:07:42] Sofia Patel: pilot typically 2-4 weeks for initial benchmark and integration, then a 6-8 week pilot in dedicated to validate SLOs. for Private on-prem, add deployment window — maybe 4-6 weeks more depending on approvals
[00:07:54] Lena Ortiz: ok good, that fits our roadmap for q2
[00:07:58] Ibrahim Noor: one more thing — observability. we need per-request cost and p95 latency per route, and an ability to tie errors back to vector index version
[00:08:09] Marcus Li: Redwood Console provides token-level cost, per-route p95/p99, model and index version tagging. we can also stream traces to your observability stack
[00:08:19] Sofia Patel: let's surface any blockers — grace?
[00:08:22] Grace Thompson: blockers: we need storage footprint estimates, security docs, and a non-prod benchmark run. also want to understand migration risk and downtime windows
[00:08:34] Sofia Patel: noted. marcus, can you take the lead on benchmarks and migration notes?
[00:08:38] Marcus Li: yes i'll draft a benchmark plan and run a sketch on Dedicated. i'll include 128/256/512/768 dims and hybrid bm25+embed flows. i'll also outline migration steps
[00:08:48] Ibrahim Noor: i'll compile current stats and send them over — index size, QPS, typical query patterns, and a sample query set
[00:08:55] Sofia Patel: great. action items and next steps we'll put in an email after this call. any other questions?
[00:09:03] Lena Ortiz: just one — do you have references with customers in regulated spaces?
[00:09:08] Sofia Patel: yes we can share a case study of a healthcare customer on Private. i'll include that in the security pack
[00:09:14] Grace Thompson: thanks everyone, this was helpful
[00:09:17] Marcus Li: thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs and schedule the SE deep dive for next week
[00:09:22] Sofia Patel: perfect, talk soon
[00:09:25] [END OF RECORDING]

Notes: transcription contains a few mis-hearings; timestamps approximate. Some numeric calc errors were corrected in follow-up email.
